title: Multi-LCB: Extending LiveCodeBench to Multiple Programming Languages
abstract: Multi-LCB addresses the limitation of LiveCodeBench by providing a multi-language benchmark for evaluating LLMs across twelve programming languages while maintaining contamination controls and evaluation protocols.

title: S-Agent: Spatial Tool-Use Elicits Reasoning for Spatial Intelligence
abstract: S-Agent is a spatial reasoning framework that enhances visual language models with temporal memory and hierarchical spatial tools to enable continuous 3D world understanding from multi-view imagery.

title: FreeStyle: Free Control of Style-Content Dual-Reference Generation from Community LoRA Mining
abstract: FreeStyle is a scalable dual-reference generation framework that uses community LoRA mining to create large-scale style-content triplets while addressing content leakage through disentanglement mechanisms and a comprehensive benchmark.

title: JanusMesh: Fast and Zero-Shot 3D Visual Illusion Generation via Cross-Space Denoising
abstract: A fast, training-free framework generates text-driven 3D visual illusions by decoupling generation into cross-space dual-branch denoising and view-conditioned texture synthesis for seamless geometric fusion and semantic coherence.

title: Current World Models Lack a Persistent State Core
abstract: Current world models fail to maintain consistent world states when unobserved, indicating a need for design changes that prioritize physical state stability over appearance fidelity.

title: LedgerAgent: Structured State for Policy-Adherent Tool-Calling Agents
abstract: LEDGERAGENT is a method for customer service agents that maintains task states in a separate ledger to improve policy adherence and state management during tool calling.

title: HumanScale: Egocentric Human Video Can Outperform Real-Robot Data for Embodied Pretraining
abstract: Egocentric human video can effectively replace teleoperated robot trajectories for embodied model pretraining, achieving better performance with reduced data collection costs.

title: The FID Lottery: Quantifying Hidden Randomness in Generative-Model Evaluation
abstract: Analysis of FID variance across different training and sampling seeds reveals significant reproducibility issues in image generation evaluation, with retraining causing larger fluctuations than resampling, and recommends updated evaluation protocols with error bars and optimal guidance tuning.

title: When the Trump administration cracks down on Anthropic, who benefits?
abstract: Listen on Apple Podcasts Listen on Spotify Anthropic recently took its two newest AI models offline due to an export control order from the Trump administration, prompting broad debates about AI policy and digital sovereignty . On the latest episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast , Sean O’Kane, Rebecca Bellan, and I discussed what actually prompted the administration’s moves against Anthropic, and what this might mean for the broader AI ecosystem. As Sean put it, “Anthropic has not had the best relationship with the Trump administration in a way that stands apart from the other leading AI labs,” so perhaps other Anthropic’s rivals don’t need to worry about a similar crackdown. But Rebecca also noted that leading cybersecurity experts have “ signed an open letter to ask Trump to revoke the order , and they say it’s actually dangerous to have to pull these advanced cybersecurity capabilities from network defenders in the U.S.” And we wondered whether this could all end up being good publicity for Anthropic, especially since — in Rebecca’s words — “everybody loves a bad boy.” Keep reading for a preview of our conversation, edited for length and clarity. Rebecca Bellan: As I’m sure many of our listeners know, the U.S. government basically just forced Anthropic to pull its two newest models offline — Fable 5, and then there was also Mythos 5, which was the one that was available to current Mythos users, [whereas] Fable 5 was more available to the public. They sent a letter [last] Friday that cited “national security concerns.” No one knows what those concerns are. That report has not been made public, they gave no specifics and told [Anthropic] that they had to ensure that those models couldn’t be used by any foreign nationals. So Anthropic was like, “Okay, I guess we have to just pull the models entirely, because we don’t know when someone’s a foreign national. title: Beyond Siri: Here are the practical AI features coming to your iPhone in iOS 27
abstract: Siri’s AI overhaul may have been the headline announcement at Apple’s Worldwide Developers Conference earlier this month, but Apple’s broader AI strategy is taking shape through a series of smaller features embedded across its software. Rather than asking consumers to adopt the new AI-powered version of Siri to get all the benefits that AI brings, the company is weaving AI into the apps and services people already use, with a focus on solving real-world problems. The result is that your iPhone will be able to split restaurant bills among friends, secure your passwords after data breaches, automate tasks, and organize information with less manual effort, among other things. Individually, these features may not be as dramatic as a Siri that finally understands your personal context and can take action on your behalf. But combined, they showcase a vision for AI that’s less about chatting with a bot and more about making Apple’s software itself feel smarter and more capable. Beyond Siri AI , here are the smaller AI features in iOS 27 that we’re most looking forward to using. The features are live now in the developer beta and will soon arrive in the public beta, before iOS 27’s general public release later this fall. Bill splitting When iOS 27 rolls out later this fall, customers will be able to split the restaurant bill using Apple Cash. Powered by Apple Intelligence, you simply take a photo of the receipt (or upload a photo), and you’ll then see a new option that lets you choose to split the bill with others. Apple Intelligence works to extract the key details from the bill, like the items ordered and the quantities, the tip, and the total. You can choose the items you ordered from the receipt and then share a request for others to do the same by messaging the group chat. Others can select their items and quantities — even selecting a half (1/2) if they split with another. To pay, you double-click just as you would for any other Apple Cash transaction. Image Credits:

title: Signal’s Meredith Whittaker wants you to remember that AI chatbots ‘are not your friends’
abstract: In Brief Posted: 1:32 PM PDT · June 20, 2026 Image Credits: TechCrunch Anthony Ha Signal’s Meredith Whittaker wants you to remember that AI chatbots ‘are not your friends’ Asked about the privacy implications of chatbots like ChatGPT and Claude, Signal President Meredith Whittaker answered, “These are not your friends. These are not conscious beings. These are not sentient interlocutors.” Whittaker made those comments in a broader interview with Bloomberg about policy, privacy, and Signal. She acknowledged that she uses AI tools “to format a document here and there,” but insisted, “I don’t ask them questions. I’m very serious about my thinking and writing, and I don’t want the process of working through an idea […] to be foreclosed or eclipsed by the response of a system that’s averaging what’s already out there.” As for Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman’s prediction that users could let Microsoft Copilot handle all their Christmas shopping this year, Whittaker argued this scenario — where Copilot is eavesdropping on the family group chat to determine who wants want — means giving it “access to my credit card, my browser, my Signal, the ability to message my siblings on my behalf, my home address [and] my calendar.” “What you’ve just described is a system with very pervasive access across multiple applications and services,” Whittaker said. “In the context of Signal, it would constitute a kind of a backdoor.” Topics AI , Meredith Whittaker , Security , signal June 18 Los Angeles Get an inside look at what it takes to scale and succeed from leaders at Mach Industries, Founders Fund, and Shinkei Systems. title: In the Weights is your new AI-centric vanity search
abstract: Anyone who’s Googled themselves recently knows that it doesn’t quite hit the way it used to. Sure, there’s everything going on with Google search itself , but there’s also an inescapable feeling that web search isn’t the canonical source of information that it used to be, with just as many people learning about who you and I might be from chatbots. Thomas Dimson and Joey Flynn had a similar feeling, leading them to create In the Weights . The “weights” in question are the numerical parameters that shape an AI model’s training and output, so the website purports to measure how well “a model is able to recall someone without using tools like web search.” “Being in the weights means your existence was deemed important in the process of creating superhuman artificial intelligence,” the website says. To achieve this, In the Weights supposedly queries different models (including Grok, Gemini, multiple versions of GPT, Claude, and Llama, plus lesser known models) with a question similar to, “Who is <name>? Give up to 10 results, each with a short description and confidence.” It then “cluster[s] similar descriptions together and assign[s] a strength score.” Image Credits: In the Weights For example, this humble tech blogger received a strength score of 641, placing me in the top 6% of names. I was feeling pretty good until I saw that multiple TechCrunch colleagues scored even higher. And the leaderboard has been shifting as I write this post, with “Home Alone” star Macaulay Culkin currently in the top slot with a strength score of 988, neck-and-neck with opera singer Luciano Pavarotti. The results also show which models returned which answers for a given name, and they highlight potential hallucinations — apparently GPT-5.4 Mini says that Anthony Ha is an “ambiguous name form that could refer to multiple people with the initials A.H.A.” Asked why he built In the Weights, Dimson told TechCrunch via email that he and Flynn were looking to “get the creative juices flowing agai

title: 具身賽道現狀素描：腦子靈，模型好，不是百億，就是獨角
abstract: 具身賽道現狀素描：腦子靈，模型好，不是百億，就是獨角 魚羊 2026-06-21 17:18:12 來源： 量子位 2026年還沒過半，具身智慧的融資就快要超過去年全年了，超過一半的錢都流入了機器人的“大腦”。 林方舟 發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號 QbitAI 具身智慧領域的資本，正在湧向機器人的“大腦”。 量子位不完全統計，2026年上半年（截至6月12日），國內具身智慧賽道共融資約438億元。而2025年全年的融資金額約554億元，2024年約137億元。照這個勢頭，2026年的融資將再創新高。 其中， 超過一半的錢湧入了“大腦派”公司 。相比於上一代以硬體為核心或全棧平臺公司，“大腦派”更強調自己用“軟體定義硬體，模型定義本體”。 而業務以機器人本體為核心的“本體派”公司，同期融資僅佔12.8%，甚至低於生產核心零部件（如巧手、感測器、關節模組等）的企業（14.4%）。 不少 “大腦派” 公司的融資速度彷彿坐上了火箭，「平均一個月融資一輪」甚至成了行業常態，最誇張的一家，兩輪融資之間只隔了兩週。 這是一個年輕的賽道。在量子位不完全統計的35家“大腦派”公司中，大多數公司（20家）處在早期融資階段（種子/天使/Pre-A輪），沒有一家公司進入後期融資階段（C/D/Pre-IPO輪）。 這也是一個火熱的賽道。量子位統計，具身大腦公司Pre-A平均融資7億元、B輪平均融資22.5億元——放在其他大多數領域，這都是C/D輪的量級。 我們總結了當下具身大腦創投的幾個重要趨勢。 具身大腦融資提速 第一個趨勢是： 具身大腦賽道的融資節奏之快，已經打破了傳統需要里程碑驗證才能推動下一輪的邏輯。 自2025年下半年開始，資本大量湧入具身大腦賽道，進入2026年後，融資節奏進一步提速。 例如，2026年1月成立的德塔智慧，3個月內便完成3輪超億元融資；同期成立的章魚動力，不到2個月，就完成數億元人民幣種子輪和近5000萬美元天使輪；眸深智慧，也在半年內完成5輪融資。類似的案例還有不少。 而且， 不少公司的融資量級，已經遠高於該輪次的基準。 它石智航在4月Pre-A輪融資4.55億美元（約合人民幣33億元），不僅創下中國具身智慧最高單輪融資紀錄，還超過了絕大多數公司的A/B輪融資額。 部分專案的天使輪，獲得資本連續加碼。 深穹星核僅用不到70天，就完成了「天使輪-天使+輪-天使++輪」三級跳；知躍空間智慧甚至拿到了「天使++++」，並在2026年4月一個月內，連續完成兩輪融資。 通常而言，天使輪主要看「想法和團隊」，而A輪會關注「商業模式和資料」。初創企業持續在天使輪融資，通常意味著業務尚未跨過下一輪標準的門檻。 同時，資源正在向頭部公司集中。融資金額排名前五的公司，合計融資154億元，約佔賽道融資總額的七成。 其中，千尋智慧是目前最受追捧的“大腦派”公司。它在2月至6月，接連完成四輪融資，累計金額近50億元，估值已高達200億元。 回頭來看，這波“大腦派”公司的創業熱潮，從2025年延續至今。量子位不完全統計，2026年至今披露過融資動態的35家“大腦派”公司中，超過一半成立於2025年以後。其中，有6家新公司創立於今年。 而機器人本體和大腦並重的“全棧派”公司，大多成立於2025年之前。 近期，一些“全棧派”公司，也靠著“大腦”能力的提升，獲得資本加註，身價暴漲，甚至晉升百億估值俱樂部。 例如，2026年3月，星動紀元宣佈完成10億元戰略輪融資，估值破百億元。其融資新聞的重點是公司在世界模型、VLA的突破和領先，及全棧自研的能力。 另一家估值破200億元的“全棧派”公司是星海圖。其合夥人兼CFO羅天奇公開表示，當前機器人行業的發展，核心變數是具身大腦的迭代。 為何具身大腦當前備受資本追捧？ 投資圈流傳著一句話： “本體兜住下限，大腦決定上限。” 有投資人告訴量子位，機器人的硬體雖然暫時還不完備，但更考驗供應鏈、成本控制、量產能力，憑藉中國的製造業優勢，機器人本體將快速進化。 而當前資本市場的共識是：大腦是具身智慧最大的難點，且天然有更高的估值邏輯——邊際成本低、可複用、可遷移。 千尋智慧創始人兼CEO韓峰濤在2026智源大會上說，如果把鋼鐵俠的賈維斯視作100分的機器人，那麼現在機械臂的技術成熟度有50分，輪式底盤有40分，四足有30分，而AI智慧化只有3分，“但從3分進步到50分的速度將會很快”。 近八成公司研發世界模型 第二個明顯的趨勢是： 世界模型已成為新融資中最受青睞的技術路線。 量子位統計，今年上

title: 2026年，1800個DeepSeek跟我一起守護艾澤拉斯
abstract: 2026年，1800個DeepSeek跟我一起守護艾澤拉斯 henry 2026-06-21 12:46:07 來源： 量子位 一個月只要340塊 henry 發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號 QbitAI 終於，也是等到了讓AI來守護艾澤拉斯的這一天。 最近，一位Reddit老哥手搓了一個《魔獸世界》私服—— 裡面活躍著 1800 個AI玩家，而且全都接入了 DeepSeek API ，能像真人一樣聊天、組隊、閒逛。 於是，暴風城的聊天頻道突然變成了DeepSeek廣場，畫風大概是這樣的： 獵人在懷念舊天賦，法師接話“奧杜爾是我最愛的副本”，旁邊還有人在吐槽“奧核之眼簡直是毒瘤”。 乍一看，跟正常的魔獸聊天頻道沒什麼區別。更關鍵的是，這套東西還特別 便宜 。 由於DeepSeek API成本極低（得益於此前的Token永久折扣），老哥透露，之前執行450個AI玩家版本時， 每天線上5~6小時，一個月API費用還不到10歐元（約85塊） 。 換算下來，1800個Bot跑滿一個月，也就340塊，一頓Omakase的錢。 該說不說，雖然這些年玩家總在吐槽《魔獸世界》里人機越來越多，但真到了私服裡，有這麼一群會自己聊天、自己互動的AI，好像又突然變得順眼了起來。 目前，這條帖子已經拿下1100多個贊、593條評論，衝上相關板塊熱帖第一。 DeepSeek這波熱度，也是成功讓暴雪蹭上了（doge）。 為了部落，為了聯盟，為了DeepSeek！ 1800個DeepSeek跟我守護艾澤拉斯 一句話概括老哥的做法： 找一個現成的私服安裝包，裡面自帶機器人模組和AI聊天外掛，再寫一個Python指令碼，把聊天介面從本地模型轉到DeepSeek的雲端API。 具體來說，安裝包用的是魔獸世界3.3.5版本（巫妖王之怒），屬於社群裡很常見的“Repack”方案，下載解壓就能直接執行。 包裡有兩個關鍵模組： 一個叫 Playerbots ，能批次生成模擬真人行為的bot，做任務、升級、組隊全自動； 另一個提供 本地大模型的聊天介面 。 由於本地跑大模型太吃硬體，老哥直接讓AI幫自己寫了一個Python橋接指令碼，把聊天請求全部轉發到DeepSeek雲端API。 為了進一步省錢，他還加了一個小最佳化：檢測到沒有真人線上時，自動停止呼叫API。 （屬於是該省省，該花花了） 整個搭建過程被他總結成一句話：改改配置檔案，複製貼上Python指令碼，然後雙擊批處理檔案啟動。 甚至連他自己都承認：“說實話，如果沒有AI幫忙，我根本搞不定這些。” 不過，這個私服看起來似乎很make sense，但有一個關鍵限制，就是： DeepSeek管嘴，Playerbots管腿，兩套系統之間沒有打通。 比如你在頻道里對一個戰士說：“幫我拉Boss。” 它可能會認真回覆你：“好的，鐵議會我最拿手。” 但說完之後，它並不會真的跑過去開怪。 所以從本質上看，這更像是一個被AI填滿的單機版《魔獸世界》。 Playerbots負責讓世界裡有人在走動，DeepSeek負責讓聊天頻道里有人在說話。 老哥一個人站在暴風城中央，和1800個AI一起守護艾澤拉斯。 By the way，由於懂得都懂的原因，老哥並不打算公開自己的私服安裝包。 （注：2025年下半年起暴雪密集起訴WoW私服，Turtle WoW、Stormforge等大服相繼在2026年5月關服，社群猜測暴雪在為BlizzCon 2026公佈Classic+清場。老哥這種純本地、不公開的單人私服，恰好處在暴雪夠不到的灰色地帶） 網際網路已死VS熱血懷舊服 針對老哥這波神人操作，不少網友也是在評論區開始激情對線。 點贊最高的一條評論（447贊）直接丟擲靈魂拷問： 這不就是死亡網際網路理論的現實版嗎？ 這裡給不熟悉的同學來點上下文。 所謂“死亡網際網路理論”（Dead Internet Theory），是近幾年越來越火的一種猜想： 互聯網裡的大部分內容和互動，其實已經不是人創造的，而是AI生成的。 通俗點就是：這遊戲還有活人嗎？ 這個問題其實挺關鍵。因為很多玩家對AI進遊戲最大的反感就在於—— AI不會破防，不會整活，不會半夜跟你激情對線，就嗯愣頭青玩自己的。 久而久之，MMO最重要的那種“活人味兒”就沒了。 但另一邊，也有不少網友覺得： 如果一款遊戲已經沒人玩了，那讓AI把它重新填滿，好像也沒什麼不好。 而且說實話，跟Claude或者DeepSeek聊魔獸，很多時候還挺有節目效果。 有人回憶起小時候沒錢買點卡的時候，總幻

title: NousResearch/hermes-agent
abstract: Hermes Agent ☤ Hermes Agent | Hermes Desktop The self-improving AI agent built by Nous Research . It's the only agent with a built-in learning loop — it creates skills from experience, improves them during use, nudges itself to persist knowledge, searches its own past conversations, and builds a deepening model of who you are across sessions. Run it on a $5 VPS, a GPU cluster, or serverless infrastructure that costs nearly nothing when idle. It's not tied to your laptop — talk to it from Telegram while it works on a cloud VM. Use any model you want — Nous Portal , OpenRouter (200+ models), NovitaAI (AI-native cloud for Model API, Agent Sandbox, and GPU Cloud), NVIDIA NIM (Nemotron), Xiaomi MiMo , z.ai/GLM , Kimi/Moonshot , MiniMax , Hugging Face , OpenAI, or your own endpoint. Switch with hermes model — no code changes, no lock-in. A real terminal interface Full TUI with multiline editing, slash-command autocomplete, conversation history, interrupt-and-redirect, and streaming tool output. Lives where you do Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal, and CLI — all from a single gateway process. Voice memo transcription, cross-platform conversation continuity. A closed learning loop Agent-curated memory with periodic nudges. Autonomous skill creation after complex tasks. Skills self-improve during use. FTS5 session search with LLM summarization for cross-session recall. Honcho dialectic user modeling. Compatible with the agentskills.io open standard. Scheduled automations Buil

title: tashfeenahmed/freellmapi
abstract: FreeLLMAPI One OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Sixteen free LLM providers. ~1.7B tokens per month. Aggregate the free tiers from Google, Groq, Cerebras, NVIDIA, Mistral, OpenRouter, GitHub Models, Cohere, Cloudflare, HuggingFace, Z.ai (Zhipu), Ollama, Kilo, Pollinations, LLM7, OVH AI Endpoints, and OpenCode Zen — plus any custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint (llama.cpp, LM Studio, vLLM, local Ollama) — behind a single /v1/chat/completions endpoint. Keys are stored encrypted. A router picks the best available model for each request, falls over to the next provider when one is rate-limited, and tracks per-key usage so you stay under every free-tier cap. freellmapi.co — browse the live model catalog Contents Why this exists Supported providers Features Not yet supported Quick start Docker Desktop app Premium (live catalog) Using the API Screenshots How it works Context Handoff Limitations Contributing Terms of Service review Disclaimer Why this exists Every serious AI lab now offers a free tier — a few million tokens a month, a few thousand requests a day. On its own each tier is a toy. Stacked together, they add up to roughly 1.7 billion tokens per month of working inference capacity, across 100+ models from small-and-fast to reasonably capable. The problem is that stacking them by hand is painful: seventeen different SDKs, seventeen different rate limits, seventeen places a request can fail. title: modem-dev/hunk
abstract: hunk Hunk is a review-first terminal diff viewer for agent-authored changesets, built on OpenTUI and Pierre diffs . multi-file review stream with sidebar navigation inline AI and agent annotations beside the code split, stack, and responsive auto layouts watch mode for auto-reloading file and Git-backed reviews keyboard, mouse, pager, and Git difftool support Split view with sidebar and inline AI notes Stacked view and mouse-selectable menus Install npm i -g hunkdiff Or with Homebrew: brew install modem-dev/tap/hunk Requirements: Node.js 18+ macOS, Linux, or Windows Git recommended for most workflows Nix users can use the default package exported in flake.nix instead. See nix/README.md for details. Quick start hunk # show help hunk --version # print the installed version Working with Git Hunk mirrors Git's diff-style commands, but opens the changeset in a review UI instead of plain text. hunk diff # review current repo changes, including untracked files hunk diff --watch # auto-reload as the working tree changes hunk show # review the latest commit hunk show HEAD~1 # review an earlier commit Working with Jujutsu and Sapling Hunk auto-detects Jujutsu and Sapling checkouts, so hunk diff [revset] and hunk show [revset] use native revsets inside jj or Sapling workspaces. To override VCS detection, set vcs = "git" or vcs = "jj" or vcs = "sl" in config . Working with raw files and patches hunk diff before.ts after.ts # compare two files directly hunk diff before.ts after.ts --watch

title: Adaptasi Jurnalis Pikiran Rakyat Media Network Bandung di Era Kecerdasan Buatan
abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed the media industry and encouraged journalists to adapt to new forms of digital collaboration. This study aims to analyze how journalists at Pikiran Rakyat Media Network Bandung (PRMN) adapt to AI in their journalistic practices, identify factors influencing its adoption, and examine strategies for maintaining journalistic credibility. This research employed a qualitative descriptive approach using data triangulation through in-depth interviews, non-participant observation, document analysis, and expert informant interviews. Data were analyzed using the Miles and Huberman model and interpreted through Rogers' Diffusion of Innovation Theory. The findings show that PRMN integrates AI into three stages of the journalistic workflow: News Collecting, News Processing, and News Publishing. AI adoption has increased productivity, accelerated content production, and expanded analytical perspectives while remaining under human editorial control. The adoption process is driven by perceived benefits, institutional support, and search engine optimization (SEO) demands. To mitigate risks, PRMN implements evaluation forums, double verification procedures, AI-content labeling, and strict adherence to journalistic ethics. The study concludes that AI serves as a supporting tool that enhances journalists' capabilities rather than replacing their professional roles, highlighting the importance of adaptive capacity in successful AI adoption.
